title: Delaware AI Laws

reading.body:
Delaware's two AI laws are both about the commission that will write AI policy, not about AI itself.

One law, HB16, passed in May 2025, amends the Delaware Artificial Intelligence Commission's statutes. It revises the definitions of artificial intelligence, commission, and generative AI, sets membership at 23 voting members, and adds a nonvoting high school student appointed annually by the chair. The other, HJR7, passed in July 2025, directs that commission to work with the Secretary of State on a regulatory sandbox for testing agentic AI, and requires a written report with findings, recommendations, and draft legislation by January 2, 2026.

The pattern is procedural. Delaware has built the body and given it a task, but has not yet enacted substantive requirements on developers or deployers. The sandbox is aimed at agentic AI specifically, which is the category of system that acts rather than only answers, and the report deadline is the mechanism by which the state's next move becomes visible.

What this data does not cover is the content of that report, any rules the sandbox will impose, or how the commission's revised definitions will be applied. It also says nothing about data centers, electricity, or siting. Nothing here indicates Delaware is regulating the physical buildout that AI compute depends on.

body_html:
Delaware has enacted 2 AI-related laws. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in Delaware

2 laws this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • HJR7: Directing The Artificial Intelligence Commission To Work In Collaboration With The Secretary Of State To Create A Regulatory Sandbox Framework For The Testing Of Innovative And Novel Technologies That Utilize Agentic Artificial Intelligence. passed 2025-07-23

    Directs the Artificial Intelligence Commission to work with the Secretary of State to create a regulatory sandbox framework for testing innovative and novel technologies that use agentic artificial intelligence, and requires a written report with findings, recommendations, and draft legislation by January 2, 2026 to specified state officials.

  • HB16: An Act To Amend Title 29 Of The Delaware Code Relating To The Artificial Intelligence Commission. passed 2025-05-13

    This Act amends the Delaware Artificial Intelligence Commission statutes. It revises definitions of Artificial Intelligence, Commission, and Generative AI, and changes Commission membership to 23 voting members. It adds a nonvoting high school student member appointed annually by the Chair.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Delaware. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
